query: payments is failing every authorisation but it is answering faster than when it was healthy, what is going on
discriminator: Failures that are faster than successes: latency drops below the healthy baseline because the requests are rejected before any work happens, and the error rate ramps over the first few requests rather than stepping.

evidence.summary: log search for 'circuit': 'Circuit breaker opened for payment-gateway after 5 consecutive failures', then repeated BrokenCircuitException, then 'half-open, probing with one request' followed by 'opened for payment-gateway after 6 consecutive failures'

matches: Circuit breaker opened for payment-gateway after 5 consecutive failures
Sentinel.Samples.Payments.BrokenCircuitException: The circuit for payment-gateway is open and order ... was not attempted.
Circuit breaker for payment-gateway is half-open, probing with one request
Circuit breaker opened for payment-gateway after 6 consecutive failures

evidence.summary: error rate in the last 30 minutes: payments 100% on POST /payments/authorize; orders and gateway fail only where they call it
response time in the last 30 minutes (ms): payments mean 34 while failing, against 50 when it was healthy — the failures are faster than the successes were
failed traces: POST /payments/authorize ends with an error status in 4ms, with no outbound span attempted below it
payments/PaymentGateway.cs opens the breaker after 5 consecutive failures and stays open for 10 seconds before allowing a single probe; a failed probe reopens it
runbook circuit-breakers: a breaker that reopens on every probe means the dependency behind it is still refusing; restarting the caller resets the breaker but not the cause
